newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria c.bank says cuts main rate to 17.14 pct.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria c.bank says cuts main rate to 17.14 pct.

text.p: The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) said on Thursday it cut its main interest rate to 17.14 percent monthly from 18 percent, in force from Monday.
It said this was in line with falling yield of short-term government securities.

"The BNB sets the central interest rate at 17.14 percent monthly, in force from April 7, based on the weighted average effective monthly yield of seven-day discount T-bills auctioned in the past five days," the BNB said in a statement.

The rate rose to 18 percent monthly from 16.50 percent on March 1 based on a combination of weighted average effective monthly yields of 17.67 percent for one-week T-bills and 19.14 percent for four-week T-bills auctioned daily by the Finance Ministry.
The weighted average effective monthly yield of one-week discount T-bills fell to 17.14 percent at the auctions held in the past five days, BNB figures showed.
The change in the calculation method was recommended under a $510 million 14-month standby accord signed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF) in mid-March.
Under the accord Bulgaria pledged to introduce in June a tough fixed exchange rate mechanism, called a currency board, to restore confidence in its collapsing financial system.

On Wednesday Finance Minister Svetoslav Gavriiski said that immediately after the introduction of the currency board system annual interest rates were expected to be set by the market and to fall to between 20 and 30 percent and to 10 percent by yearend.
The system would require levs in circulation to be matched by central bank reserves, severely curbing the financial powers of the government and the central bank and preventing the printing of money.
The BNB said it would adjust the rate bi-weekly in April basing it on the yield of seven-day discount T-bills from five successive auctions. From May the rate would be adjusted each week.

The Finance Ministry has issued daily discount T-bill issues with maturities of one week and four weeks without par value or a minimum acceptable price set in advance since January 20 to regulate excessive bank liquidity.

Since then the BNB has halted its revrepo operations with maturities of over two days in line with preparations for the introduction of a currency board under which central bank open market operations would be curbed.
Under the financial accord with the IMF repurchase agreement balances should be reduced to zero by end-May, or two weeks before the introduction of a currency board system.

Once the currency board is introduced the BNB will not be able to print levs it cannot cover with hard currency reserves, which is expected to remove political pressure from monetary policy. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 981 8569; 981 4145
